title: Virginia's 7th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Virginia's 7th Congressional District stretches across 11 localities in central and northern Virginia, including parts of Prince William, Stafford, Spotsylvania, and Culpeper counties. Incumbent Democrat Eugene Vindman, first elected in 2024 by a 2.5-point margin, is seeking a second term. Three Republicans—entrepreneur Philip Harding, retired Army Lieutenant Colonel Doug Ollivant, and pastor/construction owner Ricky Smithers—are competing in the August 4, 2026, primary to challenge him. The race takes place after a failed redistricting amendment was struck down by the Virginia Supreme Court, keeping the current map in place, and is rated 'Solid D' by the Cook Political Report.
polling_note: No independent district-level general election polls were found for VA-07 as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race 'Solid D' as of May 8, 2026.

candidates.name: Eugene Vindman
candidates.summary: Eugene Vindman is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 7th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A retired U.S. Army officer and former White House National Security Council deputy legal advisor, he came to national attention during the first impeachment of President Trump for his role in reporting the Trump-Ukraine phone call. His campaign emphasizes lowering costs for families, fighting corruption, and supporting veterans and military families.

candidates.name: Philip Harding
candidates.summary: Philip Harding is a Republican candidate and entrepreneur who founded Impact Junkie, a company helping people start businesses with over 2 million participants globally. A first-generation college graduate who earned degrees from Harvard Extension School and served as Harvard-wide student body president, he previously worked in Congress and as a senior advisor at the Pentagon and White House. His campaign focuses on reducing government regulations and taxes, strengthening families, and tackling the national debt.

candidates.name: Douglas Ollivant
candidates.summary: Douglas (Doug) Ollivant is a Republican candidate and retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel with two combat tours in Iraq, service in Afghanistan, teaching at West Point, and serving as Director for Iraq at the National Security Council. He is managing partner at Mantid International, a global consulting firm focused on combating corruption. His campaign emphasizes fiscal responsibility, rebuilding American industry, national security, and protecting rural and suburban community values.

candidates.name: Ricky Smithers
candidates.summary: Ricky (Rick) Smithers is a Republican candidate, U.S. Army veteran, construction company owner, and founder and pastor of a church. He lives in Wirtz, Virginia (outside the 7th District) and previously ran unsuccessfully for the Franklin County Board of Supervisors in 2019. His campaign focuses on affordability, public safety, education, economic opportunity, and restoring confidence in government.

forecast.rationale: No district-level general election polling is available for VA-07, so confidence is low and the forecast relies entirely on non-polling fundamentals. Incumbent Democrat Eugene Vindman won this seat by a narrow 2.5-point margin in 2024 and is seeking a second term. The district map remains in place after the Virginia Supreme Court struck down a redistricting amendment. Cook Political Report rates this seat 'Solid D' as of May 2026, indicating a strong Democratic lean. However, the narrow 2024 margin, the unsettled three-candidate Republican primary (August 4, 2026), and the total absence of polling data introduce meaningful uncertainty. The fundamentals still favor the incumbent, but the margin is unlikely to be as dominant as safer Democratic seats, supporting a 'likely D' rating with a probability in the mid-to-high 80s.
